=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): alternate (leaves are attached at successive nodes along the stem, alternating sides; no paired or whorled arrangement visible)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaves are spaced along the stem with visible internodes, not clustered at the apex)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (each leaf consists of multiple leaflets attached to a central rachis)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (leaflets are arranged along a central axis with a terminal leaflet present)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 8 (each compound leaf has approximately 7–9 leaflets; estimate of 8 based on most visible leaf)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): alternate (leaflets are arranged alternately along the rachis, not in pairs)

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): toothed, dentate (margins have small, regular teeth pointing outward, consistent with dentate morphology)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaflets are elongated with a narrow base and wider at the middle, tapering to an acute apex)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (apex is sharply pointed but not drawn out into a long tip)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (base is wedge-shaped, tapering to the petiolule)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (primary veins extend from midrib to margin, with secondary veins branching off the midrib)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, numerous (secondary veins are clearly visible, running perpendicular to midrib, closely spaced)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): glabrous, dull (surface appears smooth without hairs; not shiny, with a matte finish)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is short, supporting the compound leaf; rachis is longer)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petiole is round in cross-section, no wings or grooves visible)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears firm and slightly lignified, typical of young woody seedlings)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem surface)
    19. Stem color: green to reddish-brown (stem is primarily green with some reddish-brown tinge, especially near nodes)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface appears smooth without ridges or lenticels)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules observed at leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no exudate visible when stems or leaves are broken)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaflet base visible; not characteristic of Fabaceae)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils observed)

F. Notes: Several leaflets show minor damage including holes and margin irregularities, likely due to mechanical or environmental factors. The seedling is low-growing, with multiple compound leaves emerging from the same stem. Images show consistent morphology across angles, confirming alternate leaf arrangement and odd-pinnate compound leaves with dentate margins. No reproductive structures visible.
